boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission ways to meet up around Marion, from public trails and gardens to courts, fitness stations, and a free city bus ride.

cards.title: Walk the Cardinal Greenway
cards.subtitle: A free rail-trail outing from Marion
cards.notes: Meet near a Marion access point, choose a turnaround together, and finish before dusk; check the trail site for closure notices first.
cards.short_summary: Take a no-fee walk, run, or bike ride on Indiana’s 62-mile rail-trail.
cards.evidence_claim: Cardinal Greenways states that the trail spans 62 miles from Marion to Richmond and is free to use from dawn to dusk every day.
cards.access_notes: Open dawn to dusk every day; review the official trail-updates section before departing.

cards.title: Follow the Riverwalk
cards.subtitle: A 2.25-mile public path through Marion
cards.notes: Start at Washington Street Bridge, walk toward Matter Park, and pause at the public parks and monuments encountered along the river.
cards.short_summary: Share a paved riverside walk linking downtown Marion with Matter Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City describes the Mississinewa Riverwalk as a 2.25-mile recreational path through several public parks, beginning at Washington Street Bridge and ending at Matter Park’s pond.
cards.access_notes: Public outdoor trail; begin at Washington Street Bridge and First Street or join from Matter Park.

cards.title: Play a Disc-Golf Round
cards.subtitle: No-admission recreation inside Matter Park
cards.notes: Bring discs from home, form a small group, and play within Matter Park’s posted hours; the activity needs equipment but no purchase on site.
cards.short_summary: Turn a park meetup into a casual round on Matter Park’s documented course.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies Matter Park as 110 acres of public land, lists a disc-golf course among its amenities, and posts park hours of 7 a.m.–11 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Matter Park is open 7 a.m.–11 p.m.; bring your own discs because equipment availability is not stated.

cards.title: Meet for Pickleball
cards.subtitle: Public courts at Matter Park
cards.notes: Bring paddles and balls, divide into pairs, and rotate players between games; visit only during Matter Park’s posted operating hours.
cards.short_summary: Organize a doubles session on the city-listed pickleball courts.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies Matter Park as public land, specifically lists pickleball courts, and gives the park’s hours as 7 a.m.–11 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Matter Park is open 7 a.m.–11 p.m.; bring personal paddles and balls.

cards.title: Stroll the Gardens
cards.subtitle: Landscaped public grounds in Matter Park
cards.notes: Walk the fenced gardens and Meadow, compare seasonal plantings, and use the public seating; keep bicycles and skates outside the gardens.
cards.short_summary: Catch up among annual plantings, statues, shade structures, and the Meadow.
cards.evidence_claim: The City documents the 6.3-acre Gardens and Meadow as part of public Matter Park, with more than 7,000 annual plants, seating, statues, and garden features.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor garden access requires no admission; no smoking, skating, or bicycling, and pets must remain leashed.

cards.title: Try a Fitness-Court Circuit
cards.subtitle: Outdoor exercise at Charles Mill Park
cards.notes: Meet for a body-weight circuit, adjust movements to each person’s ability, and use the city’s linked fitness app only if it helps your group.
cards.short_summary: Build a social workout around Marion’s outdoor Fitness Court Studio.
cards.evidence_claim: The City describes Charles Mill Park as three acres of public space with a walking path, basketball court, and the Charles Mill Fitness Court Studio.
cards.access_notes: Charles Mill Park is open 7 a.m.–9 p.m.; the Fitness Court is outdoors in the public park.

cards.title: Roll at Hogin Park
cards.subtitle: A city skate park beside Cardinal Greenway
cards.notes: Bring a skateboard or skates and appropriate protective gear, take turns on features, and stay within the park’s 7 a.m.–9 p.m. schedule.
cards.short_summary: Meet for a daytime skate session in a nine-acre public park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City lists Hogin Park as a nine-acre park with a skate park, walking path, seating areas, and posted hours of 7 a.m.–9 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Open 7 a.m.–9 p.m.; bring your own equipment and use protective gear appropriate to the activity.

cards.title: Trade Reads at Barnes Park
cards.subtitle: A book-swap meetup in public green space
cards.notes: Bring an eligible book to share or browse what is present, then settle near the shelter for a group reading break during park hours.
cards.short_summary: Pair a park hang with a browse through its miniature free library.
cards.evidence_claim: The City describes Barnes Park as two acres of public green space with a shelter, playground, and miniature free library, open 7 a.m.–9 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Barnes Park is open 7 a.m.–9 p.m.; book selection depends on what community members have supplied.

cards.title: Plan a Dog-Park Meetup
cards.subtitle: Free daylight access on Pennsylvania Street
cards.notes: Bring a compatible dog, supervise continuously, and use the size-appropriate enclosure; visitors without dogs should choose another card.
cards.short_summary: Let dogs socialize in separate large- and small-dog areas while their people catch up.
cards.evidence_claim: The City reports that UltiMutt Dog Park at 140 N. Pennsylvania Street welcomes the public during daylight hours free of charge.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public during daylight hours; use the separate enclosure appropriate for the dog’s size.

cards.title: Take a Fare-Free City Ride
cards.subtitle: Explore Marion together by public bus
cards.notes: Choose a destination served by the system, check the current route and operating schedule, and board together without planning for a fare.
cards.short_summary: Make the ride part of the hang on Marion’s fare-free transit system.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Marion explicitly states that it offers free bus service through the Marion Transit System.
cards.access_notes: Bus service is free; confirm current routes, stops, accessibility needs, and operating times with Marion Transit before leaving.
